raw_result.summary: Pinned one production Web startup selector and composition entrypoint, and one target-scoped generator-certificate verifier with a controlled authenticated-certificate input source. The ordinary, authorization-only and selected-data modes are closed and fail before serving on invalid configuration; controlled WebApplicationFactory tests exercise the same Program and verifier without a test route or simulated TLS claim.
raw_result.finding_disposition: ID-R02/I06/S03/L02/T01 now name OctoberWebStartupSelector.Resolve(IConfiguration), immutable OctoberWebStartupSelection, VulgataWebComposition.ConfigureServices(builder, selection), three exact mode values and selected-data host inputs, plus OctoberGeneratorCertificateVerifier.VerifyAsync with its source, allowlist and closed decision. T006/T007 can select authorization-only mode through host configuration and supply controlled certificate identity to the unchanged verifier.
raw_result.feasibility: Current Program already creates WebApplicationBuilder and calls VulgataWebComposition.ConfigureServices(builder), then resolves readiness, migrates and maps endpoints. Resolving mode before those actions and branching the existing composition/startup path is a local Web change. Existing WebApplicationFactory tests use ConfigureAppConfiguration; the same production host key is testable. The authorized bootstrap needs no October connection or preseeded batch.
raw_result.invariants: Absent mode preserves ordinary startup. Unknown, partial or conflicting explicit mode configuration fails before October registration, migration or request service; authorization-only has exactly the two grant routes and no October context/selector/source-approval. Selected-data requires exact target, batch, fresh protected grant and existing-batch BindAsync before serving. Certificate proof never derives from a request header, cookie, body or untrusted proxy claim; the same target-scoped verifier checks all internal routes. A valid certificate alone never substitutes for operator grant/current authority.
raw_result.async_failure_retry: The certificate source and concrete verifier forward cancellation and return only Authorized, Unauthenticated, Forbidden, AuthorityUnavailable or Cancelled. Missing/invalid certificate is 401, authenticated out-of-target identity is 403, authority/configuration outage is 503; no cached allow or mode fallback exists. Startup failure serves no October request. Fresh activation grant is still required on restart; immutable host selection does not become a reusable disclosure capability.
raw_result.migration_compatibility: The ordinary Web service, readiness, Identity/domain migration and endpoint path remains its default branch. Authorization-only uses ordinary Identity/Data Protection and management authority but never registers, opens or migrates an October target. Selected-data requires an already committed exact batch and never migrates; generator prepare alone retains empty-target migration after live authority and connected-target identity. No schema, source-tool, provider or later-story contract changes.
raw_result.constitution_architecture: Core setup and Story 18.1 source contracts remain unchanged; Web owns TLS/auth and Identity, Infrastructure owns October persistence. This preserves Constitution I/III/V, the accepted fixed-database October architecture and the PRD. The correction adds no Worker tool, Scan strategy, route, PRD change or external resource permission.
raw_result.test_seam_and_limits: A SelfContained WebApplicationFactory can supply the same October:Web:Mode key and controlled IOctoberAuthenticatedCertificateSource plus immutable target/fingerprint allowlist; it does not replace OctoberGeneratorCertificateVerifier or add a test endpoint. Such tests establish composition and authorization decisions only; T020/T029 still require separately authorized real TLS/certificate, process and PostgreSQL qualification.
raw_result.implementation_design_shape: Architecture classification, front matter, required headings and all existing design IDs are retained. The installed deterministic plan-content validator returned no errors and git diff --check passed. Root owns path/hash-bound lifecycle validation after mapping.
raw_result.planned_change_and_gate: This is a callable clarification of the already approved three-mode bootstrap and mTLS target-scope semantics, not a new trigger or substantive product choice. The existing plan-authorization-01 scope remains semantically applicable, but this self-review does not rebind approval to changed hashes, accept an independent review, restore implementation approval, change recovery counts or authorize tests/code/resources; root controls those gates.
